## 449ea8b9619c

**No issue found in the checked semantic/validator domain.** This task recolors
the connected shape using its unique bottom-left marker and removes the marker.
I checked the retained canonical inputs, deterministic generated cases, actual
Racket labels, the task's Python mirror, malformed-marker/color cases, and its
seven existing focused tests in the portable runtime.

Measured: **300/300 valid, deterministic and nonidentity samples**, with Python
mirror/Racket parity on all 300. All three retained canonical pairs matched and
were accepted. The 300 calls contained 200 unique grids; this is recorded rather
than presented as 300 independent unique examples. That duplicate count is not a
proof of a label or validator defect, nor is this audit a broad diversity approval.

Four concrete mutation checks were rejected for the expected reasons: missing
marker, repeated marker, missing shape, and an extra nonmarker color. Exact
messages are in `checks/audits.json` → `audits.449ea8b9619c.mutation_rejections`.
All seven existing focused tests passed as part of the 59-test portable run in
`checks/portable-final.json`.

Scope: the declared one-shape-color/unique-marker envelope. I did not expand the
audit to arbitrary unsupported color multiplicities and claim they were valid
training cases. No universal correctness or train-safety claim follows from this
finite check.
